Subject: Request: short-term throughput uplift for sprint launch (Nov 12-14)

Hi Lauren,

We're ramping an external marketing sprint that will drive a burst of inference traffic for our recommendation API. We expect a 6-8x traffic increase between Nov 12 00:00 UTC and Nov 14 23:59 UTC (3 days) for a set of peak windows. Can Redwood provide a temporary throughput/top-up for that window?

Key asks:
- Immediate short-term QPS/throughput lift for the three-day window.
- Favorable overrun pricing or a small launch credit — we are a committed customer but this is a one-off campaign.
- A clear procurement path (PO + invoice timing) so we can get finance sign-off by Monday.

We can be flexible on commitments; we'd prefer a blunt short-term uplift and a pro-rated invoice rather than renegotiating the annual commit. If there's an option to convert the burst into a month-long temporary commit at a blended rate, we're open to that too.

Attaching our expected traffic matrix and a PO template. Please loop in pricing/legal if needed.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Platform
OptiPark, Inc.
(sara.m@optipark.com)

Hi Sara — thanks for the details and the matrix. Important note: Ben is on the pricing/ops side and Markus owns runtime capacity. I've summarized options below; Ben will follow up with rates and a quote spreadsheet. Markus, can you confirm capacity availability and any technical caveats about warm pools or cache priming?

Initial options we can offer (high-level):
1) Short-term burst (3-day uplift) charged at a blended overrun rate with a launch credit (we can offer 20% on overrun tokens as a one-time concession). Pro-rated invoiced after the window.
2) Temporary month-long commit (Nov full month) at a reduced effective rate that amortizes the uplift — requires PO that covers that month.
3) Escrowed buffer: purchase a burst credit bucket upfront (prepaid) that applies only to Nov 12-14. This avoids post-run reconciliation but requires payment before the window.

If any of these look promising Sara, Ben will send a precise quote and a redlined PO flow for finance/legal to review.

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a short quote workbook (redwood-burst-pricing-quote-nov2026.xlsx) that lays out three concrete options with estimated spend, effective per-token/unit rates, and invoice timing. High level summary below:

Option A — Pro-rated overrun (post-run true-up)
- Short-term uplift applied automatically; tokens beyond monthly threshold billed at overrun rate $0.045/1k tokens (post-run).
- One-time launch credit: 20% applied to the overrun amount (not cumulative).
- No PO required in advance; we invoice after reconciliation (Net 30).

Option B — Prepaid burst bucket (recommended if you want cost certainty)
- Purchase a prepaid burst bucket for the expected uplift volume at $0.036/1k tokens. Remaining unused credits roll into next month (valid 30 days).
- Requires PO and payment before the uplift window.

Option C — Temporary month commit (Nov)
- Convert expected uplift to a one-month elevated commit at a blended rate $0.031/1k tokens. Requires PO that covers the commit and a brief contract amendment.
- Pro: lowest effective rate. Con: requires more procurement lead time.

Technical caveats from Markus (summarized):
- Warm pools can reduce cold-start latency; we can pre-warm a modest set of instances if you give final traffic windows 48 hours ahead.
- Prefix caching recommended for heavy repeated prompts to cut token consumption.

Next steps I suggest: Sara, indicate preferred option (A/B/C) by EOD Monday and attach preferred PO template. If you choose B or C, we'll send a DocuSign + invoice steps; if A, we'll confirm reconciliation cadence and logging.

Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
